evidence.clarity: 1440 first screen: H1 'Periodic KYC reviews that hold up when the examiner asks.' plus a lede naming due-selection, gathering what is on file and asking only for what is missing, and 'Built for credit unions with 20,000 to 200,000 members.' evidence.fit: The examiner tension is handled well: a 'Questions your examiner will ask' grid with six examiner questions and where each answer lives, a dark band 'The risk decision stays with your compliance officer', and 'Where Refresh is today' covering unnamed pilots and no results. Member-service staff, who the brief says use it daily, only appear as 'Done by Refresh, checked by member-service staff' tags in the five steps and get no view of their own.
evidence.distinctiveness: The hero artifact is product-specific: a review-file ledger with hand-drawn pencil ticks, a red cross for stale data, a circled-tick decision mark, a signature-style 'Dana Whitfield', and a legend of marks. Below it the page uses the usual SaaS sequence: comparison table, numbered steps with a side card, a dark two-column band of tick lists, a 2x3 FAQ grid, a status table and a CTA band.
evidence.proof: 1440: the sample review file sits right of the headline in the first viewport, tagged 'Sample', and runs from selection to decision with dates. It is internally consistent (last reviewed Nov 2025, 12-month cycle, due Nov 2026). It is static: nothing responds, so a visitor can't step through it. At 390 it starts at y≈650 and only its header is above the fold.
evidence.craft: Steady spacing and a clear sans/serif pairing (Avenir/Segoe stack for heads, Charter stack for body). The fonts are not embedded, so the type varies by machine. The header 'Book a demo' is 37px tall. The operator's 1440-top shot catches the decision mark half-drawn (a stray stroke in the Oct 10 row) because the tick animation runs for about 3s. Otherwise no clipping or overlap at 1440, 768 or 390.
evidence.mobile: 390: the layout stacks cleanly, there is no overflow, and the comparison table becomes labelled 'Today / With Refresh' blocks, which is a real recomposition. 'See how a review runs' is 26px tall. The artifact is mostly below the first screen.
evidence.honesty: The hero file carries a 'Sample' tag in its header at every width. The status block says plainly 'Measured results: None yet' and 'Two credit unions, unnamed at their request'. The 'What the member sees' request mock ('We have Lakeview Logistics from 2021', 'This takes about two minutes') has no sample label where it appears; that disclosure is only in the footer line. The disclosure also comes as a section listing what is missing, not alongside the claims.
evidence.interaction: There is almost nothing to operate. I clicked 'See how a review runs' at 1440 and 768 and it scrolled to #how (top 0). All three 'Book a demo' links go to https://refresh.example/demo. Tab order is logical, with a 3px outline at every stop. The main artifact is a static figure, and the member mock has a styled 'Update my details' span that looks like a button but does nothing.
evidence.copy: Specific and calm, in the compliance officer's vocabulary: 'What was already on file, and how current was it?', 'Your compliance officer, not Refresh', 'they have asked us not to name them, so there are no logos on this page'. The closing ('Bring your review policy and we will run it under your cycles') says what the demo involves. A few sections cover the same ground: what Refresh does and doesn't do is restated in the steps, the dark band and the Q&A.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific promise, sample file and 'Book a demo' all in one viewport. Member-service staff, the daily users, get no section or view of their own, and below the hero the structure falls back to a stock SaaS sequence (comparison table, steps, dark band, FAQ grid, CTA band).

evidence.clarity: H1 'KYC reviews your examiner can follow', then a bold first line of the lede: 'Refresh is periodic KYC review software for credit unions with 20,000 to 200,000 members.' Category, audience and job are stated in two lines, with 'Book a demo' directly below at 1440, 768 and 390.
evidence.fit: Every audience in the brief has its own path. 'For BSA officers' covers policy tiers and 'What stays with the officer'. 'What members see' has a sample request to Marisol. 'For member services' has a sample work queue for staff. 'At exam time' covers the trail. The demo's trail tags each entry Refresh / Staff / Member / Officer. 'Refresh never sets a risk rating; your compliance officer does' sits under the hero CTA, and the pilot and no-results facts are stated without a 'what we lack' section.
evidence.distinctiveness: The page is organised by the product's own five stages ('1–2 Due, On file', '3 Asked', '4 Checked', '5 Decided'), and each section is tagged with its stage chip. The demo puts the same member's spreadsheet row beside the Refresh file ('due?', 'called 10/13, left voicemail', 'binder to be built before exam'), which makes the replacement visible. Condensed Heros headlines and role chips give it a forms-and-ledger feel. The envelope/phone line drawing in 'Asked' is more decorative than useful.
evidence.proof: The operable sample file sits in the first viewport at 1440. I stepped through all five stages. Member details move from 'Not gathered yet' to 'On file' / 'Missing' to 'Requested' to 'Checked' plus 'Risk rating: Medium, unchanged', and the audit trail grows from 1 to 7 entries. The numbers agree across the page: 24-month medium tier in the demo and in the policy table, photo ID expired March 2026 in the demo and in Marisol's request, next review due Oct 2028.
evidence.craft: Embedded Heros and Heros Cn fonts give a sharp type scale (68/46/22px at 1440) and consistent chips and rules. Minor defects: at 1440 the demo card grows from 701px to 1062px as you advance, which pushes the page below. At 320 the 'Checked' and 'Decided' chip labels touch their cell edges. The '3 Asked' section at 1440 has a small request card and a large drawing with a lot of empty space around it.
evidence.mobile: 390: 'Menu' (44px+) opens a full-width list with a full-width 'Book a demo'. Escape closes it and returns focus to the button, and tapping 'For member services' closes the menu and scrolls to the section. The demo is recomposed into stacked panes, and the stage tabs stay as a five-up row. The readout updates directly above 'Next stage', so feedback lands where you tap. No targets under 44px and no overflow at 390 or 320. At stage 5 the card is about 1660px tall at 390.
evidence.honesty: Every example is labelled where it appears: 'Sample written for this page; the member, staff and dates are invented.' in the demo header, 'Sample review policy, for illustration', 'Sample request to member 20417, written for this page.', 'Sample list for Thu 15 Oct 2026, written for this page.' The final CTA note reads 'Opens our booking page.' The pilot and no-results facts appear in the hero note and in the FAQ.
evidence.interaction: Next stage steps through stages 1–5. At stage 5 it disables and relabels to 'Review closed', and focus moves to 'Start over'. 'Start over' returns to stage 1. Clicking the '2 On file' chip jumps there directly. Arrow keys on the radio chips moved the stage, and the readout is aria-live. New trail entries are highlighted. All four FAQ details opened. No console errors at any width, and every stop had a 3px focus outline.
evidence.copy: Concrete and in the customer's world: 'found by filtering the sheet by date', 'A member with nothing missing goes straight to the officer, with no request at all', 'No binder to build the week before.' Button labels say what they do. Two FAQ answers fall back on 'Covered in the demo' (data hosting, core systems) where a compliance officer wants at least a one-line answer.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific promise, named audience, 'Book a demo', the pilot and risk-decision note, and the working sample file all in one viewport. 390: headline, audience lede, CTA and pilot note are in view, plus the demo's sample label and stage tabs at the bottom edge. The readout itself is just below the fold.

problems: The demo card changes height at every stage (701px to 1062px at 1440, up to about 1660px at 390), which moves everything below it and makes the hero feel unstable while you operate it.
Two examiner-critical FAQ answers (where data is held, which core systems) just defer to the demo, which is thin for a compliance buyer.
Uneven composition in the middle: the '3 Asked' section pairs a small request card with a large decorative envelope/phone drawing and dead space, and at 320 the stage chip labels crowd their cells.

reason: B shows the product doing its job in the first screen. A visitor can step one sample member from due to decided, see the spreadsheet it replaces and watch the audit trail build, and the rest of the page is organised around those same stages, with a real path for officers, staff, members and examiners. A has excellent examiner-facing copy and a beautiful static ledger, but nothing to operate, a phone layout without navigation, and no view for member-service staff. A working, equally honest interactive version of A's file would make this much closer.
